look_for: Starts from what the customer needed, gathers their feedback, and makes a tradeoff in their favor.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you went out of your way to understand what a user or customer actually needed.
followups: How did you find out what they needed?
What did you change because of it?
How did you know it helped them?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to choose between what was easiest for you and what was best for the people using your work.
followups: What did the easier option look like?
What did choosing the harder one cost you?
What was the outcome for the user?

look_for: Acts beyond their job description, thinks long term, and doesn't say 'that's not my job'.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you took on something that wasn't your responsibility because you saw that it needed to get done.
followups: What exactly did you do yourself, as opposed to the rest of the team?
How did you measure the result?
Looking back, what would you do differently?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you made a decision that was better for the long term even though it cost you something in the short term.
followups: What was the short-term cost?
How did you convince others it was worth it?
How did it turn out over time?

look_for: Finds a new or simpler way, looks outside for ideas, and is fine with being misunderstood for a while.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you found a simpler way to do something that others were doing the hard way.
followups: Where did the idea come from?
Did anyone push back? How did you handle it?
How much did it actually save?

questions.q: Tell me about something you built or proposed that was genuinely new for your team or class.
followups: What problem was it solving?
What did you try that didn't work?
What happened to it after you shipped it?

look_for: Makes good calls with incomplete data, seeks out different views, and works to disprove their own beliefs.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to make an important decision without all the information you wanted.
followups: What information was missing?
How did you reduce the risk of being wrong?
Was it the right call? How do you know?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you changed your mind after hearing a different point of view.
followups: What did you believe at first, and why?
What convinced you?
What did you do differently afterwards?

look_for: Teaches themselves new things quickly and is curious about possibilities beyond the task.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new technology or skill quickly to get something done.
followups: How did you go about learning it?
What was hardest to pick up?
How do you use it now?

questions.q: Tell me about something you explored on your own just because you were curious.
followups: What sparked it?
What did you find out?
Did it change how you work?

look_for: Helps others grow: mentors, gives useful feedback, and raises the bar of the people around them.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you helped a teammate or classmate get better at something.
followups: How did you figure out what they needed?
What did you do, step by step?
How did they improve?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you gave someone difficult feedback.
followups: How did you prepare for the conversation?
How did they react?
What changed afterwards?

look_for: Holds a high bar for quality, fixes problems so they stay fixed, and doesn't ship something they know is broken.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you weren't satisfied with something that others thought was good enough.
followups: What exactly wasn't good enough?
What did raising the bar cost in time?
Was it worth it? How do you know?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you found a problem in your own work after you thought you were done.
followups: How did you find it?
What did you do about it?
What do you do now to catch it earlier?

look_for: Proposes a bold direction, communicates it, and looks for ways to have a bigger impact.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you turned a small task into something with much bigger impact.
followups: What made you see the bigger opportunity?
How did you get others on board?
How far did it get?

questions.q: Tell me about the most ambitious goal you've set for a project.
followups: Why that goal?
What got in the way?
How close did you get, and what did you learn?

look_for: Moves quickly when a decision is reversible, takes calculated risks, and doesn't wait for perfect information.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had a tight deadline and couldn't get everything done. How did you decide what to cut?
followups: Who set the deadline, and did you push back on it?
What did you leave out, and what happened because of that?
How did you tell the people affected about the tradeoff?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you took a calculated risk to move faster.
followups: What was the risk, and why was it acceptable?
What would you have done if it went wrong?
What was the result?

look_for: Gets more done with less: works within limits on time, money, or people, and finds resourceful ways around them.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to get something done with far fewer resources than you wanted.
followups: Which resource was missing?
What did you do instead?
What did you have to give up?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you saved time or money for your team in a way nobody asked for.
followups: How did you notice the waste?
How much did it save?
Did it stick after you left?

look_for: Listens, speaks candidly, admits mistakes openly, and treats others respectfully.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to rebuild trust with someone after something went wrong.
followups: What broke the trust?
What did you do to rebuild it?
How did you know it was rebuilt?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you had to tell someone something they didn't want to hear.
followups: Why did it need to be said?
How did you say it?
How did they respond, and what happened next?

look_for: Stays connected to the details, audits with data, and digs until the root cause is clear.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you used data to find the real cause of a problem that others had missed.
followups: What data did you look at, and why that data?
What surprised you?
How did you confirm it was the root cause?

questions.q: Tell me about a mistake you made on a project. How did you find it, and what did you change afterwards?
followups: How did you track down the root cause?
What did you change so it wouldn't happen again?
What did you learn from it that you still use?

look_for: Respectfully challenges decisions they disagree with, with evidence, and then commits fully once a decision is made.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate or a manager about a technical decision.
followups: How did you make your case? What data did you use?
What happened in the end, and how did you feel about the outcome?
If the decision went against you, how did you commit to it?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you committed to a decision you didn't agree with.
followups: What did you disagree with?
How did you make sure it still succeeded?
Looking back, who was right?

look_for: Focuses on the key inputs, delivers with the right quality on time, and doesn't settle when setbacks happen.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you hit a major setback but still delivered.
followups: What was the setback?
What did you change to still deliver?
What did you deliver in the end, and was it on time?

questions.q: Tell me about the project you're proudest of delivering.
followups: What was your personal part?
What nearly made it fail?
What impact did it have, in numbers?

lp: Strive to be Earth's Best Employer
look_for: Makes the environment better for the people around them: safer, more inclusive, more supportive.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you made a team or group a better place to work for someone else.
followups: What wasn't working for them?
What did you do about it?
How did it change things?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you noticed a teammate struggling and did something about it.
followups: What did you notice?
How did you approach them?
What happened afterwards?

lp: Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility
look_for: Thinks about second-order effects of their work on users, the community, and the world, and acts responsibly.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you thought about how your work could affect people beyond its intended users.
followups: What effect were you worried about?
What did you change because of it?
How did you check it worked?

questions.q: Tell me about a time you raised a concern about privacy, accessibility, or fairness in something you worked on.
followups: What was the concern?
How did others react?
What was decided, and what was your part?
